The Independent — Pol Allingham — "British man and wife 'killed in Athens building collapse' after explosion near the Acropolis" — 26 Sep 2026, 14:20 BST

A British man and his Greek wife are believed to be among those killed in a building collapse near the Acropolis in Athens, according to local media reports.
Rescue workers retrieved six bodies following an explosion in the Plaka tourist area on Friday morning, as reported by Greek broadcaster ERT.
The UK national and his spouse were reportedly in their 70s and resided on the second floor overlooking the Hadrian's Gate monument. American tourists staying in a short-term holiday let on the first floor also died, ERT reported.
The blast was likely caused by a massive gas leak, Athens mayor Haris Doukas said on Friday night.
Search teams equipped with cameras, sensors and rescue dogs recovered the bodies, fire brigade spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis confirmed in a televised briefing.
A police source said the tourists, two American couples, had been due to catch a 3pm flight from Athens airport on Friday but failed to appear. Investigators from the fire service's crime unit are on site amid reports of a gas smell in the district.
Rubble and shattered glass were flung up to three blocks, damaging nearby houses, shops and vehicles.
